accounts.name: Standard STP (Vantage International / global site)
accounts.account_currency_unit: USD (also GBP, CAD, AUD, EUR, SGD, NZD, HKD, JPY)
accounts.max_leverage: Up to 1:1000 on the main site (eligible countries, equity-dependent). The APAC help centre says 1:100-1:2000 and the global help centre says 100:1-500:1. Retail ASIC/FCA is capped at 1:30.
accounts.server_time: GMT+2 standard / GMT+3 during DST, so server midnight = 17:00 New York close
accounts.notes: 'From' spread conflicts between Vantage pages: the STP page says from 1.0 pip, the accounts overview says from 1.1. TYPICAL: Vantage's own EURUSD guide says about 1.2 pips typical on Standard. Third-party measurements: ForexBrokers.com found a 1.4 pip average, and Myfxbook shows a 1.13 pip average with the account type unspecified. Vantage's live-spread page showed a snapshot of 13.69 for Standard STP vs 0.69 for Raw. These look like points (about 1.37 vs 0.07 pips), but the unit was not confirmed. Plan on 1.2-1.4 pips typical, wider at rollover and news. Margin call 50% / stop-out 20% have applied to STP and ECN accounts since 9 Feb 2025 (not UK or Australia). Lot step is not published (check the MT5 symbol spec). EAs are allowed without restriction unless used for 'exploitative or suspicious' activity. Hedging is allowed on MT5; on a fully hedged position the margin offsets, but Vantage may close hedged positions it considers abusive. The client agreement lists 'scalping' as wilful misconduct only where it exploits thin liquidity, wider-than-usual spreads or off-market pricing. EURUSD swap is not published on the website; it is visible only in MT5 Specification, with triple swap on Wednesday.

accounts.name: Raw ECN (Vantage International / global site)
accounts.account_currency_unit: USD (also GBP, CAD, AUD, EUR, SGD, NZD, HKD, JPY)
accounts.max_leverage: Same as Standard STP: up to 1:1000 on the main site (eligible countries, equity-dependent), 1:100-1:2000 per the APAC help centre, 100:1-500:1 per the global help centre
accounts.server_time: GMT+2 standard / GMT+3 during DST, so server midnight = 17:00 New York close
accounts.notes: Commission is USD 3.00 per standard lot per side (USD 6 round turn), which is 6 cents round turn on 0.01 lot. Commission is charged in the account base currency. Vantage does not publish a typical/average Raw EURUSD spread. The 0.13 typical figure is ForexBrokers.com's measured 0.127-pip average, an all-in cost of about 0.72 pips including commission. A legacy Vantage help article gave 0.1 pip as the Raw EURUSD minimum. The live-spread page snapshot showed '0.69' for Raw, unit unclear (probably points, about 0.07 pips). For a $100 grid/scalping EA, the all-in cost of about 0.7 pips per round turn usually beats Standard STP's 1.2-1.4 pips. Hedging, EA and scalping caveats are the same as Standard STP. EURUSD swap is not published on the website (see MT5 Specification).

accounts.name: Pro ECN (Vantage International / global site)
accounts.max_leverage: Not stated separately. The help centre says 'all account types' get 100:1-500:1 (global) or 1:100-1:2000 (APAC).
accounts.notes: Requires a USD 10,000 deposit and a request to support@vantagemarkets.com (open trades must be closed first), so it is not reachable with $100. Vantage markets it as suited to 'day traders, scalpers, and expert advisors'. No typical spread is published; it presumably uses the same raw feed as Raw ECN, but this is unverified. Minimum lot is not stated explicitly for Pro ECN.

accounts.name: Cent (MT5 only for new accounts)
accounts.account_currency_unit: USC (US Dollar Cent): $100 shows as 10,000 USC
accounts.max_leverage: Not published on Vantage's Cent page. A third party (DayTrading.com) reports 1:500. The help centre says 'all account types' get 100:1-500:1 (global) or 1:100-1:2000 (APAC).
accounts.notes: Help centre: minimum deposit USD 50, trades only in USC, minimum lot 0.01. New Cent accounts can no longer be opened on MT4; open an MT5 Cent account through the client portal or the app. Vantage's Cent page variously says 'open with $1' and 'trade from $50', and advertises 'spreads from 0.0'. The same site also says the only difference from Standard STP is the cent denomination, which implies STP-style commission-free pricing. Vantage does not explicitly publish Cent commission or typical spread. DayTrading.com reports commission-free and an average of 0.2 pips EUR/USD, which is unverified and looks optimistic. Margin call and stop-out are assumed from the help centre's 'stop-out level on all trading platforms is 20%'. A cent-lot contract size is not published: check the MT5 Specification for contract size and volume step before sizing a grid. A third party says the Cent account carries only about 90 instruments. No swap-free Cent variant was found.

accounts.name: Swap-Free / Islamic (variant of Standard STP, Raw ECN, Pro ECN)
accounts.account_currency_unit: USD (minimum 50 units of account currency, 400 HKD or 5000 JPY)
accounts.notes: Offered on STP, Raw ECN and Pro ECN. Spread and commission follow the underlying type, so 'from 0.0' applies to the Raw-based version and 0 commission to the STP-based one. Swap is replaced by an administration fee on overnight positions; Vantage does not publish the fee amount or a grace period. A '2.5 basis points' figure in the client agreement refers to futures-CFD rollovers, not swap-free. Officially only for clients who cannot pay or receive interest for religious reasons. Vantage may revoke accounts it believes abuse swap-free status (carry trades, arbitrage). The help-centre list also names a 'Premium Swap Free' type.

accounts.name: Premium (MT4 only)
accounts.max_leverage: 2000:1 (varies with equity and around news or market open and close)
accounts.notes: Not usable for an MT5 EA: Vantage says Premium is MT4-only. Minimum deposit is USD 500-3000 depending on country. Margin call 30% / stop-out 0%. Includes 20% off swap rates. Commission is unclear: the 'plus' Premium pages mention USD 1.00-1.50 per side tiers tied to $10k-$150k deposits.

accounts.name: Premium Unlimited (launched 11 Mar 2026)
accounts.max_leverage: Up to 1:2,000,000,000 ('unlimited'), dynamic by equity: 0-5k USD unlimited, 5k-30k 1:2000, 30k-100k 1:1000, above 100k 1:500. Leverage is reduced around market open and news.
accounts.notes: Minimum deposit is USD 500-3000 depending on country, so it is not reachable with $100. Eligibility requires at least 10 trades and 3+ lots of volume. A 0% stop-out applies 'in select markets'. Commission-free and spreads from 0.1 come from the regional vantagemarketsea.com page, which lists MT4/MT5. Margin call level is not published.

official.entity_notes:
The values above are for the offshore/global offering at vantagemarkets.com. It is run by Vantage Global Limited, regulated by the VFSC in Vanuatu (Reg. 700271), whose client agreement is dated August 2025. Clients may also be booked with Vantage International Group Ltd (CIMA, Cayman, SIBL 1383491), Vantage Markets (Pty) Ltd (FSCA, South Africa, FSP 51268, client agreement December 2025) or a Mauritius/VIG entity. The entity you are assigned depends on your country of residence.

Leverage on these offshore entities: the main site says leverage starts at 100:1 and goes up to 1000:1 depending on equity, for eligible countries only. The APAC help centre says 1:100-1:2000 for all account types; the global help centre says 100:1-500:1. Third-party summaries give the per-entity maximum as roughly VFSC 1:2000, FSCA/CIMA/FSC 1:1000. Since 9 March 2025, indices and oil use fixed margin, capped at 500:1.

Margin call / stop-out of 50% / 20% applies to STP and ECN accounts from 9 Feb 2025, explicitly excluding UK and Australian clients. Premium (MT4) uses 30% / 0%, and Premium Unlimited has 0% stop-out in select markets.

ASIC (Vantage Global Prime Pty Ltd, AFSL 428901, vantagemarkets.com/en-au): retail leverage is capped at 30:1 on major FX, with a mandatory 50% margin close-out and negative balance protection. The account names differ: 'Standard' (from 1.0 pip, no commission, $50 minimum) and 'RAW'. RAW Classic is about AUD/USD 2.5 per lot per side and RAW Premium about 1.0 per side for active traders.

FCA (Vantage Markets UK, vantagemarkets.co.uk): retail leverage 1:30 and 50% stop-out.

Server time for all entities is GMT+2, or GMT+3 during US daylight saving, so server midnight equals 17:00 New York.
official.caveats:
1) Research method: WebFetch was blocked by the network egress proxy for every domain tried (www.vantagemarkets.com, vantagemarkets.com, prnewswire.com, edubourse.com). Every value comes from WebSearch result extracts of the cited URLs, not from reading the tables first-hand. The search results occasionally contradicted each other, for example Standard STP 'from' at 1.0 vs 1.1, and leverage at 500 vs 1000 vs 2000. Re-check the key numbers in a browser before relying on them.

2) Vantage publishes 'from' spreads only. The single own-site 'typical' figure is about 1.2 pips on Standard (EURUSD academy guide). The Raw typical (0.127) and Standard average (1.4) are ForexBrokers.com measurements. The Myfxbook 1.13 average does not name the account type.

3) No EURUSD swap long or short values are published on the website. They are visible only in MT5 under Market Watch > Specification, with triple swap on Wednesday. The swap-free admin fee is also not quantified publicly.

4) Cent account: Vantage does not publish commission, typical spread, leverage, contract size or volume step for it, so those fields are -1. Third parties say it is commission-free with about 1:500 leverage. New Cent accounts are MT5-only. For a $100 grid EA, check the Cent symbol's contract size and step in MT5 before sizing.

5) Rules for a grid/hedge EA: EAs are allowed and MT5 accounts are hedging-mode. Fully hedged positions offset margin, but you still need free margin to open the hedge leg. The client agreement allows Vantage to close hedged positions it deems abusive. It lists as misconduct scalping that exploits thin liquidity or wider-than-usual spreads, sniping, latency or off-market arbitrage, and trading the gap with over-leveraged positions before market close or announcements. Trading credits or bonuses cannot be used for hedging. Ordinary scalping and EAs are marketed as fine, especially on Pro ECN.

6) Sizing for $100: at 1:500, one EURUSD lot needs about $216 margin, so 0.01 lot needs about $2.16. A 20% stop-out on a $100 account leaves little room for a deep grid. Raw ECN costs $0.06 round turn per 0.01 lot plus about 0.1-pip spread, about 0.7 pips all-in, versus about 1.2-1.4 pips on Standard STP. Pro ECN ($10k), Premium ($500-3k, MT4-only) and Premium Unlimited ($500-3k) are out of reach at $100.

7) Leverage can be cut automatically around market open, close and major news. Margin requirements and conditions vary by entity and country and can change without notice.

accounts.name: Standard STP
accounts.account_currency_unit: USD (other base currencies like EUR, GBP, AUD are offered depending on entity)
accounts.max_leverage: Up to 1:1000 under VFSC (TradersUnion leverage page). Other reviews say 1:500 (investingoal) and the broker-wide maximum is 2000:1. FCA and ASIC retail: 1:30.
accounts.server_time: GMT+2 (winter) / GMT+3 (US DST). Server midnight lines up with the 17:00 New York close, and swap is charged at the rollover with a triple swap on Wednesday.
accounts.notes: Typical EURUSD spread from independent tests: 1.4 pips average (ForexBrokers.com 2026, DayTrading.com 2026, CompareForexBrokers 2026). Live tools vary: FXVerify shows 1.35 in one snapshot and 1.51 in another. CompareForexBrokers' UK test gave 1.18. TradersUnion (Sep 2026) gives about 0.9, which is an outlier. The 'from' spread is 1.0. There is no commission because the cost is in the spread. Margin call 50% / stop-out 20% has applied to STP and ECN accounts since 9 Feb 2025 (EduBourse; TradingFinder, Sep 2026). Older reviews still quote 80%/50%, which is the pre-2025 or FCA figure. Min lot 0.01 (investingoal, TradingFinder). Max trade size on EURUSD is 100 lots (ForexBrokers.com). No independent source states the lot step: it is probably 0.01, so check SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP in MT5. EAs, hedging and scalping are allowed with no minimum hold time (EAFunded 2026, InvestingLive). The swap figures (-8.07 long / +3.94 short USD per lot per night) are low confidence: the search snippets attribute them to TakeProfitApp and CompareForexBrokers (2026). TradersUnion, BrokerChooser and TakeProfitApp snippets also quote about -2.50 long / +0.10 short, which conflicts. Another snippet gives -6.75 / +3.06. Swaps change with interest rates, so read the live values from MT5 Specification. For a hedged 1:1 grid, the net swap is roughly long + short, which is negative (about -4.1 USD per lot per night using the -8.07/+3.94 pair). For a $100 account this is the 'simple' option, but its cost is about 1.4 pips against about 0.8 pips all-in on Raw ECN.

accounts.name: Raw ECN
accounts.account_currency_unit: USD (other base currencies depending on entity)
accounts.max_leverage: Up to 1:1000 under VFSC (TradersUnion). Some reviews say 500:1 (investingoal, fxscouts). FCA and ASIC retail: 1:30.
accounts.server_time: GMT+2 (winter) / GMT+3 (US DST), New York close.
accounts.notes: Measured raw EURUSD spread, excluding commission: 0.127 pips average (ForexBrokers.com 2026), 0.12 at the London-NY overlap (TakeProfitApp 2026), 0.23 average with a 0.18 snapshot (CompareForexBrokers 2026), about 0.2 (DayTrading.com 2026), about 0.3 (TradersUnion, Sep 2026) and 0.08 on a UK live account (CompareForexBrokers UK, Jul 2026). FXVerify's live tool shows 0.83 pips including commission, which is about 0.23 raw. BrokerChooser (Sep 2026) lists 0.0 at peak hours. I used 0.2 as the typical value; the range is 0.13 to 0.3. Commission is $3.00 per lot per side ($6 round turn) on offshore and global entities (BrokerChooser, ForexBrokers.com, CompareForexBrokers). UK Raw ECN pricing differs: CompareForexBrokers cites $2.00 round turn there. All-in cost is about 0.72 to 0.8 pips per round turn. Per 0.01 lot that is about $0.06 commission plus about $0.02 spread, roughly $0.08 per round turn, compared with about $0.14 on Standard STP. Reviewers rate it the best Vantage account for EAs, and HFT and scalping are allowed (EAFunded). Free VPS is available to clients who meet balance and volume thresholds. MC 50% / SO 20% since 9 Feb 2025. Lot step is not independently published (probably 0.01). Swap values are low confidence, as for Standard STP. Best fit for the $100 grid/scalping EA.

accounts.name: Pro ECN
accounts.max_leverage: Not independently published for this account type. TradersUnion says leverage depends on entity: VFSC up to 1:1000, FCA and ASIC 1:30.
accounts.notes: Requires a $10,000 minimum deposit, so a $100 trader cannot open it. Raw pricing is the same as Raw ECN (TakeProfitApp), so I used the same typical spread of about 0.2. Commission is $1.50 per side ($3 round turn) per ForexBrokers.com, CompareForexBrokers, TradersUnion and DayTrading.com. Investingoal says $2 per side and TakeProfitApp says $1.50 to $2, so it may vary by entity. MC 50% / SO 20% applies because EduBourse and TradingFinder say the levels cover all STP and ECN accounts. swap_free_available is set to false only because no independent source confirms a Pro ECN swap-free variant (sources name STP and RAW only).

accounts.name: Cent
accounts.account_currency_unit: USC (US cents). A $50 deposit shows as 5,000 cents.
accounts.max_leverage: Conflicting: up to 1:2000 (DayTrading.com cent page, InvestorTrip), 1:500 (FXLeaders). Only available through offshore entities (CIMA/VFSC) and in some regions.
accounts.notes: Independent data on the Cent account is thin and contradictory. Minimum deposit is $50; some sources say you can open with $1 but need $50 to trade live (DayTrading.com, TradingFinder, CompareForexBrokers). Spread: DayTrading.com and FXLeaders say 'from 0.0, commission-free' and mention about 0.2 average on EURUSD in their tests. That average is probably the broker-wide or Raw figure, not specific to the Cent account. SAShares lists Standard STP and Cent together at 'from 1.4' with $0 commission. Investingoal says cent commission is '$0 to $6.00 round turn', which suggests an STP-style and a RAW-style cent variant may exist. So the typical spread is not published (-1). If the account is commission-free, expect STP-like spreads of about 1.0 to 1.4 pips. I could not independently confirm the current margin call and stop-out. Older and generic reviews quote 80%/50%, while STP/ECN accounts moved to 50%/20% in Feb 2025, so this is reported as unknown (-1). Swap is charged in USC and no independent source publishes values. swap_free_available is set to false only because no independent source mentions a swap-free cent variant. Min lot is 0.01 cent-lot, which equals 1,000 cent units, roughly $0.01 per pip. That gives a $100 account much finer position sizing for a grid. Hedging is allowed per general Vantage policy; one review says so explicitly for Cent. Check MT5 support for Cent in the account opening portal; reviewers list MT4 and MT5.

accounts.name: Standard STP Swap-Free (Islamic)
accounts.notes: Swap-free version of Standard STP. There is no swap; instead an administration fee is charged once a position has been held for a set number of days. The fee is the liquidity provider's fee plus an internal processing fee of about 10%, it varies, and no independent source publishes the amount or the number of days (SAShares, Investingoal). Vantage also says it does not warrant Shariah compliance. The 0 swap values mean no swap but an unknown admin fee, so do not treat holding costs as zero. TradersUnion says swap-free is available to all traders. Spread, commission and margin settings are assumed to match Standard STP.

accounts.name: Raw ECN Swap-Free (Islamic)
accounts.notes: Swap-free version of Raw ECN. The admin fee works the same way as on the Standard STP swap-free account: it replaces swap after a holding period, varies, and its amount is not published independently. A hedged grid that holds positions for days would pay this fee instead of swap. Pricing is assumed to match Raw ECN ($3 per side).

accounts.name: Premium / Premium Unlimited (offshore only)
accounts.notes: Only for clients of the offshore entities (CIMA/VFSC). Minimum deposit is $500 to $3,000 depending on country, so a $100 trader cannot open it. Reviewers report MC 30% / SO 0%. FXScouts says 'unlimited' leverage means about 2000:1 in practice. Typical spread and commission are not independently published; one review lists $0 commission for Premium (SAShares). swap_free_available is set to false only because no independent source confirms a swap-free variant. Included only for completeness.

thirdParty.entity_notes: The values above are for Vantage's offshore and global entities, which is where a $100 retail client outside the UK, EU and Australia is normally placed: Vantage International Group Ltd (CIMA, Cayman) and Vantage Global Limited (VFSC, Vanuatu). Vantage Markets (Pty) Ltd (FSCA, South Africa) and other offshore licences have similar conditions. On these entities, Standard STP and Raw ECN open from $50, Raw ECN costs $3 per side, Pro ECN costs $1.50 per side and needs $10,000, and the Cent and Premium/Premium Unlimited accounts are available. Leverage under VFSC goes up to about 1:1000 (TradersUnion), up to 1:2000 on Cent/Premium, and some reviews say 1:500. From 9 Feb 2025, STP and ECN accounts use margin call 50% / stop-out 20% (EduBourse, TradingFinder). Index and oil CFDs moved to fixed 500:1 leverage in March 2025 (EduBourse); this does not apply to EURUSD. FCA (Vantage Markets UK): retail leverage 1:30, margin call 80% / stop-out 50%; CompareForexBrokers cites $2 round turn for UK Raw ECN, and the Cent and Premium accounts are not offered. ASIC (Vantage Markets Australia): retail leverage 1:30 with the mandatory 50% margin close-out. Older reviews quoting '80% margin call / 50% stop-out' as broker-wide reflect FCA or pre-2025 settings. Server time is GMT+2 in winter and GMT+3 during US DST on all entities, with midnight at the 17:00 New York close. The MT5 server you are assigned shows which entity you are on.
thirdParty.caveats: 1) How the data was gathered: WebFetch was blocked by the network egress proxy for every domain tried (brokerchooser.com, tradersunion.com, myfxbook.com, forexbrokers.com, takeprofitapp.com, fxverify.com, brokeranalysis.com). Every value therefore comes from WebSearch result summaries of those pages, not from reading the pages directly. Treat exact decimals (0.127, 0.23, 0.83, -8.07/+3.94) as reported but unverified, and check them against the cited URLs. 2) Source dates: BrokerChooser (2026; snippet cites Sep 2026 data), TradersUnion fees (Sep 2026), TradingFinder (Sep 2026), ForexBrokers.com (2026 review), CompareForexBrokers (2026), CompareForexBrokers UK (Raw spread test Jul 2026), DayTrading.com (2026), TakeProfitApp (2026), EAFunded (2026), Investingoal (2026), SAShares (updated 2026), FXScouts (2026), EduBourse (early 2025; the change took effect 9 Feb 2025), WikiFX (Feb 2025), FXVerify (live tool, snapshot date unknown, seen Oct 2026). 3) Typical vs 'from' spread: Raw ECN typical EURUSD is about 0.13 to 0.3 pips raw (I used 0.2), or about 0.8 pips all-in with the $6 round-turn commission. Standard STP typical is about 1.35 to 1.4 pips. 'From 0.0' and 'from 1.0' are marketing minimums. Spreads widen at rollover (around 00:00 server time) and on news, which matters for a scalping or grid EA. Myfxbook's live Vantage EURUSD spread page (https://www.myfxbook.com/forex-broker-spreads/vantage/6052,1) exists, but I could not read its values. 4) Swaps conflict across sources (-8.07/+3.94, -6.75/+3.06, -2.50/+0.10 USD per lot per night) and change with interest rates. For a hedged BUY+SELL grid the net swap is negative in all versions (long cost is larger than short credit), with triple swap on Wednesday. Read the live values in MT5 (Symbol > Specification). Vantage's own swap page was not used, per the independent-sources rule. 5) Lot step is set to -1 because no independent source states it. MT5 forex symbols are almost always 0.01, but confirm SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP. Max lot on EURUSD is reported as 100 (ForexBrokers.com). 6) Cent account data is weak and contradictory (spread basis, commission, stop-out, leverage). Confirm on the MT5 Cent server before relying on it, though its 0.01-cent-lot granularity is the strongest risk-control tool for a $100 grid. 7) Hedging: Vantage lets you open opposite (locked) positions even without free margin. I found no independent source stating the exact hedged-margin rate, so check margin usage on a demo. 8) Practical read for $100 plus a hedged grid/scalper EA: Raw ECN, offshore entity, about $0.08 all-in per 0.01-lot round turn, MC 50% / SO 20%. At 1:500 to 1:1000 leverage, a 0.01-lot EURUSD position needs only about $1.2 to $2.3 margin, so stop-out comes from equity drawdown, not margin. Use a Cent account if finer sizing is needed and its conditions check out. Vantage's own help-center pages (global.vantagehelpcenter.com) also describe the 50%/20% levels and the GMT+2/+3 server time, but they were not used as primary sources.

backtest_models.name: vantage_raw_ecn

backtest_models.evidence: Commission: both reports agree on USD 3.00/side ($6 round turn), from Vantage's commission page and help centre (https://www.vantagemarkets.com/trading/fees/commission/, https://global.vantagehelpcenter.com/hc/en-us/articles/10949122099599), confirmed by ForexBrokers.com, BrokerChooser and CompareForexBrokers. Spread: Vantage publishes only 'from 0.0'. The official report used ForexBrokers.com's measured 0.127 average (https://www.forexbrokers.com/reviews/vantage). The third-party range is 0.08 to 0.3: CompareForexBrokers 0.23, FXVerify about 0.23 raw, DayTrading about 0.2, TradersUnion about 0.3. I chose the more costly 0.2; run a stress test at 0.3. All-in cost is about 0.8 pips per round turn. Stop-out 20% and margin call 50% for STP/ECN since 9 Feb 2025: Vantage help centre (https://global.vantagehelpcenter.com/hc/en-us/articles/10948711085839) and EduBourse agree. Leverage: published values conflict (500 / 1000 / 2000). I used 500, the global help centre's figure and the most conservative offshore value. Min lot 0.01 in both reports. Lot step is unpublished, assume 0.01. Swap: Vantage publishes none, so these are third-party values with low confidence (see the conflicts list). Triple swap on Wednesday; server time GMT+2/+3.

backtest_models.name: vantage_standard_stp
backtest_models.account: Standard STP (MT5, offshore/global entity), USD base, min deposit $50
backtest_models.evidence: Commission is 0 in both reports (https://www.vantagemarkets.com/trading/accounts/stp/). Spread: Vantage's EURUSD academy guide says about 1.2 typical (https://www.vantagemarkets.com/en/academy/trading-eurusd/). Third-party measurements: ForexBrokers.com, DayTrading.com and CompareForexBrokers 1.4; FXVerify 1.35 to 1.51; Myfxbook 1.13 (account type not stated); TradersUnion 0.9 (outlier). I chose the more costly 1.4. The 'from' spread is listed as 1.0 on the STP page and 1.1 on the accounts overview. Stop-out 20% / margin call 50% since Feb 2025 (Vantage help centre, EduBourse). Leverage 500 is the conservative choice among 500, 1000 and 2000. Min lot 0.01; EURUSD max 100 lots. Swap: same third-party values as Raw ECN, low confidence.

backtest_models.name: vantage_cent
backtest_models.account: Cent (MT5 only for new accounts, offshore entities), USC base: $100 = 10,000 USC, min deposit $50
backtest_models.evidence: Vantage's definition (https://global.vantagehelpcenter.com/hc/en-us/articles/10574015709327-What-is-a-Cent-account): the account trades only in USC, minimum deposit $50, minimum lot 0.01. Vantage also says the only difference from Standard STP is the cent denomination. Vantage does not publish contract size, commission, typical spread or leverage for Cent. The usual cent convention is assumed: 1.0 cent-lot = 100,000 base units with P&L in USC. Under that convention, EURUSD pays 10 USC/pip per cent-lot (= $0.10), so 0.01 cent-lot = 0.1 USC/pip (= $0.001). All per-lot values here are USC per cent-lot, numerically the same as the STP USD-per-lot values. Commission: 0 USC. This is implied by Vantage ('STP in cents') and stated by DayTrading.com/FXLeaders; Investingoal hints at a '$0-$6 RT' RAW-style variant. Spread: Vantage advertises only 'from 0.0'. DayTrading's 0.2 average probably reflects the Raw account; SAShares lists Cent with STP at 'from 1.4'. I used STP-like 1.4. Stop-out: 20% comes from the help centre's 'all trading platforms' statement; the third-party report gives no current value (older reviews say 50%). Run a sensitivity test at 50%. Leverage: 1:500 (DayTrading/FXLeaders, help centre) vs 1:2000 (DayTrading cent page, InvestorTrip). I chose 500. Swap is unpublished; STP values are assumed, applied as USC per cent-lot. Confirm contract size, SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP and swaps in the MT5 Specification.

backtest_models.name: vantage_raw_ecn_swapfree
backtest_models.account: Raw ECN Swap-Free / Islamic (MT5), USD base, min deposit $50; officially only for clients who cannot pay or receive interest for religious reasons
backtest_models.evidence: Both reports say pricing follows the underlying Raw ECN account ($3/side, typical spread 0.2 as above) and that swap is 0 but replaced by an administration fee after a holding period. Neither Vantage (https://www.vantagemarkets.com/trading/accounts/swap-free/) nor third parties (SAShares, Investingoal) publish the fee amount or the grace period. Both reports warn not to treat holding cost as zero, so the unknown-cost placeholders -7/-1 are used instead of 0/0. Vantage may revoke swap-free status if it suspects abuse, such as carry or arbitrage.

backtest_models.name: vantage_standard_stp_swapfree
backtest_models.account: Standard STP Swap-Free / Islamic (MT5), USD base, min deposit $50; religious-eligibility restriction
backtest_models.evidence: Same pricing as Standard STP (0 commission, 1.4 typical spread, the conservative choice over Vantage's 1.2). Swap is replaced by an unpublished admin fee (Vantage swap-free page; SAShares/Investingoal say LP fee plus about 10%). The unknown-cost placeholders -7/-1 are used rather than 0.

backtest_models.name: vantage_pro_ecn_reference
backtest_models.account: Pro ECN (MT5), USD base, REFERENCE ONLY: min deposit $10,000 by request to support, not reachable with $100
backtest_models.evidence: Commission: Vantage says USD 1.50/side ($3 RT) (help centre article 10949122099599, https://www.vantagemarkets.com/trading/accounts/pro-ecn/), backed by ForexBrokers, CompareForexBrokers, TradersUnion and DayTrading. Investingoal says $2/side and TakeProfitApp says $1.50-2. Following the rule to prefer Vantage for commission, $3 RT is used. Spread: Vantage publishes none; the third-party report assumes the same raw feed as Raw ECN, about 0.2. Min lot: Vantage does not state it; third parties say 0.01. Stop-out 20% (all STP/ECN accounts). Swap-free availability: Vantage says yes; the third-party report could not confirm it.

conflicts: Standard STP typical EURUSD spread: Vantage academy says about 1.2 pips; ForexBrokers.com, DayTrading.com and CompareForexBrokers measure 1.4; FXVerify shows 1.35-1.51; Myfxbook 1.13 (account unspecified); TradersUnion 0.9 (outlier). I chose 1.4, the more costly value.
Standard STP 'from' spread: the STP page says 1.0, the accounts overview says 1.1. This is a marketing minimum and is not used in the backtest.

Raw ECN typical raw spread: the official report used 0.13 (ForexBrokers measurement; Vantage publishes only 'from 0.0'); third-party measurements range 0.08-0.3 (CompareForexBrokers 0.23, FXVerify about 0.23, TradersUnion about 0.3). I chose 0.2; stress test at 0.3.
Vantage's live-spread page snapshot (13.69 STP / 0.69 Raw) has unconfirmed units. It is probably points (1.37 / 0.07 pips), so it is not used.

Max leverage (offshore): main site up to 1:1000 depending on equity; global help centre 100:1-500:1; APAC help centre 1:100-1:2000; third parties 1:500 / 1:1000 / 1:2000. I chose 1:500, the conservative value. FCA/ASIC retail is 1:30, a different entity.

EURUSD swap: Vantage does not publish it on the website (MT5 Specification only). Third-party values conflict: -8.07/+3.94, -6.75/+3.06, -2.50/+0.10 USD per lot per night. I chose a deliberately pessimistic mix: the costliest long (-8.07) with the smallest short credit (+0.10), giving a net of about -7.97 per hedged lot-pair per night, triple on Wednesday. Replace with live MT5 values.
Margin call / stop-out: Vantage and EduBourse say 50%/20% for STP/ECN since 9 Feb 2025 (excluding UK/AU); older and generic reviews quote 80%/50% (pre-2025 or FCA). I used 20%.

Cent stop-out: the official report assumes 20% from the help centre's 'all platforms' statement; the third-party report lists it as unknown and notes older 50%. I used 20%; run a sensitivity test at 50%.
Cent leverage: 1:500 (DayTrading/FXLeaders, help centre range) vs 1:2000 (DayTrading cent page, InvestorTrip). I chose 1:500.

Cent spread/commission: Vantage advertises 'from 0.0' but says Cent equals STP in cents; DayTrading reports a 0.2 average, commission-free (probably a Raw figure); SAShares lists Cent at 'from 1.4'; Investingoal says '$0-$6 RT', which may mean a RAW-style cent variant. I modelled STP-style: 0 commission, 1.4 pips.

Cent contract size: Vantage does not publish it. The third-party report says 0.01 cent-lot is about $0.01/pip, but the standard cent convention (100k units, P&L in USC) gives 0.01 cent-lot = 0.1 USC/pip = $0.001/pip. These differ tenfold; verify in the MT5 Specification.
Cent min deposit: the Vantage Cent page says both 'open with $1' and 'trade from $50'; the help centre says $50.
Pro ECN commission: Vantage and most reviews say $1.50/side; Investingoal says $2/side; TakeProfitApp says $1.50-2. I used Vantage's $1.50/side ($3 RT).
Pro ECN swap-free: Vantage lists Pro ECN as eligible; the third-party report found no independent confirmation.
Premium platform: Vantage says MT4-only; the third-party report marks it MT5. Excluded either way (min deposit $500-3000).
Raw ECN commission by entity: offshore/global is $6 RT; CompareForexBrokers cites $2 RT for the UK (FCA) Raw ECN; ASIC RAW is about AUD/USD 2.5/side. The models assume an offshore entity.
Swap-free admin fee: both reports agree it exists but is unpublished, so the unknown placeholders -7/-1 are used instead of 0/0.
Data quality: both research passes had WebFetch blocked and worked from search-result snippets, so exact decimals are unverified.
recon.summary_for_user:
I built 5 backtest models for Vantage accounts you can open with $100: Raw ECN, Standard STP, Cent, and swap-free versions of Raw ECN and STP. Pro ECN is included for reference only, because it needs $10,000. Every model uses 1:500 leverage, 20% stop-out and a 0.01 minimum lot. Where the sources disagreed I took the more costly value.

- **Raw ECN looks cheapest for a scalping or grid robot.** It charges $6 per round-trip lot plus a typical 0.2-pip spread, about 0.8 pips in total.
- **Standard STP has no commission but a typical 1.4-pip spread.** Vantage's own guide says 1.2; independent tests measured 1.4.
- **The Cent account uses 10,000 units** ($100 shown as cents) and is modelled like Standard STP: no commission and a 1.4-pip spread. Costs are in cents per cent-lot. Vantage doesn't publish the contract size, commission, spread or leverage for Cent, so check its symbol settings in MT5 first.
- **Vantage doesn't publish overnight swap fees.** I used a deliberately pessimistic -8.07 long / +0.10 short per lot per night from conflicting third-party figures. Replace these with the live numbers from MT5's symbol Specification.
- **The swap-free accounts use placeholder holding costs (-7/-1)**, because the admin fee that replaces swap isn't published.

All figures come from search-result summaries, because direct page reads were blocked. Check the key numbers on a demo account before trusting the results.
